title: Regency Wraps 100% Cotton Ultra Fine Natural Cheese Cloth, 9 sq.ft 36" X36" 1pc, Chef Grade for Basting Turkey, Canning, Straining, Cheesemaking
description:
NATURAL ULTRA-FINE CHEESECLOTH: Made of 100% unbleached heavy-weight cotton, this chef-grade Regency cheese cloths is lab-tested food safe with no metals, bleach, or dyes. Pack of 1 with 9 sq ft for all your cooking needs
FOOD GRADE CHEESECLOTH: With a tight weave of grade 90, use this cheese cloths for straining soups and sauces, basting turkey and poultry, steaming vegetables, and making cheese, yogurt, nut milk, and kombucha
VERSATILE CHEESECLOTH: This cheese cloths is not only great for cooking but also for canning fruits and veggies, poaching fish, steaming food, wrapping citrus, crafting ghosts and cobwebs, decorative table runners, gift wraps, and curtains
LINT-FREE CLEANING CLOTH: This cheese cloths makes cleaning mirrors and windows easy and is perfect for dusting and polishing. Made in the USA, this cheesecloth is also excellent for protecting plants and finishing furniture
OVEN SAFE BUT KEEP AWAY FROM FLAME: Our cheese cloths is safe to use in the oven but avoid the open flame. It can be gently hand washed with soap and water but we recommend single use to avoid cross-contamination
reviews_5s:
Last night I was melting down some beeswax caps mixed with honey to make my own beeswax bar, and I ordered this product to be my filter as the last step in the process.

I used about half of this whole package of cheese cloth folded up over an empty and washed out milk carton and secured it with a rubber band (see photo). I forgot to take a picture of all the stuff that stuck to the top of the cheesecloth that didn't make it through the filter but it really worked at seperating the honey and wax from the debris. I was left with a nice clean chunk of beeswax that seperated from the honey while I let it sit over night.

Now I'm not super familiar with cheesecloth so this could be normal, but the edges were a little frayed. Nothing some scissors couldn't fix if I was worried about it, but the edges weren't going to be near my wax anyways so it was okay. Also, 9 square feet was smaller than I thought! I measured it though, and it really is 9 square feet.

Over all I would recommend this cheesecloth, it worked great even with some super hot and thick beeswax (that stuff is like hot glue!!) And was able to give me a nice clean chunk of wax as a result.Used this item to cover the turkey during roasting. It held up through hours of baking and basting. Turkey turned out great!Growing up in Chinese culture I've always loved drinking sweet soy milk but I stopped after my favorite place that made their own soy milk/tofu in Chinatown NYC closed down. Recently I got into making my own soy milk using dried soy beans and it's been an awesome experience. However my soy milk would always have some of the left over soy bean grinds in my drink which got kind of annoying despite how many times I strained it with my sieve. I finally decided to purchase this cheesecloth which is huge so I fold it up four times and use it to filter out all the soy bean grinds in my soy milk and it's been perfect, I haven't found any soy grinds in my drink anymore. My only gripe with this item is that it can be hard to clean completely sometimes and getting each and every little bit is too much of a hassle for me so I just leave it. I also implore everyone who uses it to wash it right away as if you let it sit for too long the smell really gets absorbed into the cloth and then you gotta let it soak for awhile in soap to get rid of any lingering smells. Overall I am happy with the purchase and if I ever need a cheesecloth again I wouldn't hesitate to buy another one.This is my favorite natural cheesecloth so far, so I'm inspired to write a review. One problem I've had with natural cheesecloths is that several brands have fairly large holes, even if they are labeled fine. The "ultra fine" designation on this one is actually accurate. This morning in making almond milk I doubled the cheesecloth out of habit and it was so fine that the milk didn't strain through at all. From now on I will be using just a single thickness of this product for most uses!

The price of $5 for a 9 inch square is a bit higher than other brands, but I will save money by not needing to double it. I usually use a square about 6 inches by 6 inches, so I expect to get about 18 uses out of it--or about 27 cents per use.

For my purposes that's cheap enough. For those who use a lot of cheesecloth, you might consider buying in bulk at a fabric store or online fabric retailer.

Many readers may already be here because they want a natural cheesecloth. For those used to "conventional" bright white supermarket cheesecloth, I'd like to note that this is muslin beige color. I prefer natural cheesecloth since I see no reason to put bleach in the environment as this color is just as nice as the white. I also find the idea of bleach having been on the fabric unappetizing, though I'm sure it's all washed off.This cheese cloth was the best option I could make. I used this to cover my turkey for Thanksgiving and not only did it bake phenomenally, but it helped keep and maintain the flavor of a sixteen pound bird! This is by far the best cheese cloth to invest in for a multitude of purposes.I recently started the paleo diet in hopes to jump start some weight loss and help with inflammation. It's really easy to do you pop some cauliflower in the blender, add a little water to help it mash, and blend until smooth. You remove it from the blender and stick the mix onto the cheese cloth. You roll it up making sure no ends are open or you will lose your mash and you squeeze it over the sink or into a bowl. This helps keep your mash together and remove any excess liquid in it. The cheese cloth is HUGE (about 15"x32") so it makes it so easy to use! The fine grits of the mash did not get through and I was left with a nice mash. TINY AND MADE IN CHINA.
DESPITE COUNTY OF ORIGIN IN THE DESCRIPTION USA,
YES, YOU GUESSED IT.I bought this to strain vegetable juice before a colonoscopy, so that I wouldn’t digest any large fiber particles. I washed it in boiling water and keep repeatedly rinsing it, and no matter how much I rinse this there is still lint (or cloth pieces) coming off that I certainly would not want to consume. I am not sure where the lint is coming from — e.g. from the frayed ends only or from the fabric as a whole. Perhaps if it is from the frayed edges, I should have purchased cheese cloth that has sewn seams? I do not understand the positive reviews, unless the reviewers don’t mind eating lint or are planning on using this for non-culinary purposes.This cheesecloth is junk! I bought this cheese cloth to go over my turkey, normal cotton cheesecloth absorbs moisture from the bottom of the pan pulls it up over the bird as it's cooking to keep it moist. And when you baste it it absorbs the juices to keep the bird moist.
This cheesecloth did not soak up any moisture when you put moisture over the top it rolled off in beads. This was some form of cheap polyester or some man-made material this is not cotton don't waste your money!I bought this cheesecloth to make "paneer" (a soft ricotta-like Indian cheese) and while this cheesecloth worked well for the first 2 or 3 times that I made paneer, the last time that I made paneer, it was a total disaster!

Because instead of straining out the water & retaining the cheese curds, this cheesecloth allowed the cheese curds to squeeze through the mesh right along with the water, not only wasting alot of the cheese curds, but also leaving the remainder soggy & water-logged, and basically creating such a big mess (with cheese curds and water everywhere) that I had to toss the entire cheesecloth (and whatever cheese curds that were "stuck" to it) out in the garbage can.

I guess you "get what you pay for" and that for this price its probably too much to expect that this cheesecloth would last for more than couple instances of use. Lesson learned. Next time I'll probably spend a little more to get a sturdy QUALITY cheesecloth that can be used and reused over & over without going bad!

Because this cheesecloth was an utter disappointment! :(

☆ 1 STAR!!!!!!!!!!!Got this for use in my cheesemaking hobby. Used it for straining some curds from whey. Then, threw it in the washing machine to clean it before the next use. When it came out, it had shrunken horribly and was almost useless. It had deformed and bunched up. Stretching it by hand made it cover about one quarter of its previous area, but only when I pulled it taut. If I let go, it wadded up again. It is practically useless!

Note that I have a different cheesecloth that I have been using for years that is the same size, and have been treating the same way, that does not have these issues.

This one is likely to go in to the trash. What a waste.Click to play video

So if you use these on anything with oil you are gonna have your clean-up prolonged. So I would not buy these again.Cheese cloth is already difficult to wash, but this one knots together and since the ends are unfinished it rips apart. So I cut it into 3 pieces, which made it useless for the reason I bought it.
